title: IdP variance catalog: SAML attribute & behavior mapping for RBAC v2, admin controls, and audit logs
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Create an IdP-specific compatibility catalog that documents observed SAML assertion variants from Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, and Ping; define deterministic RBAC v2 attribute mapping heuristics; prescribe audit logging fields and retention guidance; and capture admin control integration notes for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Scope:
- Produce a behavior matrix enumerating attribute names, multi-value encodings, group/role semantics, signature/certificate variations, clock-skew behavior, and common edge cases per IdP.
- Recommend a canonical attribute mapping for RBAC v2 (email, external_id, group_names, role_claim, org_unit) plus fallbacks.
- Define audit events for SSO lifecycle (login, mapping, conflict, cert_rotation, logout) and required fields.
- Surface admin UX notes: how role bind/unbind flows behave when IdP-supplied attributes change, and guidance for manual overrides in the console.
- Deliverables: compatibility catalog doc, mapping migration script (dry-run mode), test matrix and automated integration tests, and a Confluence design page plus a GH PR with implementation.

High-level mapping heuristics (canonical):
- principal_email -> SAML attribute priority: (1) email, (2) mail, (3) http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress, (4) NameID (if format=emailAddress).
- external_id -> SAML attribute 'sub' or 'uid' or NameID (preserve original format).
- group_names -> attributes: 'groups' (multi-valued), 'memberOf' (semicolon/CSV fallback), 'roles' (if present). Decode tokens where IdP encodes group arrays in JSON.
- role_claim -> attributes explicitly named 'roles' or 'x-redwood-roles' (string or CSV). If absent, map groups -> roles via configured group->role bindings.
- org_unit -> Azure AD 'department' or Okta 'organization' attribute.

IdP-specific notes (summary):
- Okta: tends to send groups as multi-valued <AttributeValue> elements; sometimes uses a URI attribute name (e.g. http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/claims/groups). Okta supports pushing group membership via Group Push; watch for nested groups being flattened. Default NameID may be 'urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress'.
- Azure AD: often emits 'groups' as GUIDs in large tenants (requires graph lookup to resolve names when over the group claim size limit). Beware of token chunking and claim 'hasgroups' behavior; our mapping must detect GUIDs and optionally call lookup when tenant integration mode enables it.
- Google Workspace: tends to use 'email' or 'sub'. Groups commonly omitted in SAML assertions; recommend using SCIM for groups or using Google Groups Sync. Multi-valued attributes are sometimes encoded as a single CSV string — implement robust CSV and JSON parsing.
- Ping: vendors often include fully-qualified attribute names and may sign assertions with different algorithms (rsa-sha256 vs rsa-sha1); ensure signature algorithm acceptance is explicit and cert rotation is tested.

Edge cases and recommendations:
- Attribute name collisions: prefer explicit attribute mappings in org-level SSO settings; fall back to canonical heuristics only when mapping not configured.
- Clock skew: default tolerance 120s for Hosted; allow configurable up to 300s for Dedicated/Private but log warnings above 120s.
- Certificate rotation: support multiple active certs and include cert_fingerprint in audit events; recommend a pre-rotation test flow and a 48-hour overlap period.
- Large group lists: when group claim > 10k characters, detect truncation/overflow and mark 'group_truncated' in audit event. Offer guidance to customers to switch to group sync or SCIM.
- Ambiguous identifiers: if both 'sub' and 'email' exist and do not match, create a 'mapping_conflict' audit event and pause auto-bind of RBAC role until manual review (console flag to override).

Audit events (required fields):
- sso.login: timestamp, user_email, idp, assertion_id, request_id, outcome, ip, cert_fingerprint, raw_attribute_keys (list), mapped_roles (list).
- sso.mapping_applied: timestamp, user_id, idp, mapping_version, mapped_roles, source_attribute_names, action (auto/manual), request_id.

2026-03-11 -- Michael Chen: Ran instrumentation on staging and captured SAML samples from Okta, Azure, Google, Ping integrations. Observed three different encodings for group lists (multi-valued, CSV, JSON payload). Added parsing heuristics to the spec.

2026-03-12 -- Priya Rao (security review): Flagged certificate algorithm acceptance and requested explicit opt-in for rsa-sha1; suggested adding a cert rotation audit event. Marked security_review_required=true.
2026-03-12 -- Michael Chen: Added audit schema and console override UX notes. Draft PR opened with mapping dry-run implementation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3142

2026-03-13 -- QA (Jorge Alvarez): Scheduled end-to-end tests for 2026-03-17. Test matrix includes: Okta multi-valued groups, Azure group GUIDs + lookup, Google CSV groups, Ping certificate rotation scenario.

audit_event_schema: fields: details|string (freeform, include reason for conflict)
test_plan_summary: Automation: 12 integration tests covering each IdP + negative cases. Manual: 3 customer-simulated flows for large group sets and cert rotation. Acceptance: mapping dry-run produces zero 'mapping_conflict' events for existing customers in staging; audit events contain cert_fingerprint and mapped_roles. QA owner: Jorge Alvarez.
observability_notes: Add per-tenant SSO mapping metric (counter) labeled by idp, mapping_result (applied/conflict), and mapped_role_count. Create an alert for mapping_conflict rate > 0.5% over 1h for high-traffic tenants. Surface recent sso.cert_rotation events in Console Admin -> Security timeline.
